theme: Beelzebul; the rich fool; fear God; the narrow door
readingInstruction: Read Luke 11:14-13:21. Conflict with the crowds and the Pharisees, warnings about hypocrisy and greed, the call to be ready, and parables of the kingdom. Read it with the question, “What do I treasure?”
settingTheScene: On the road to Jerusalem the opposition grows. Some accuse Jesus of casting out demons by Satan. Others demand a sign. Jesus speaks sharply to the Pharisees and lawyers, then turns to the crowds and his disciples with teaching on fear, money, and readiness. These chapters are full of warnings, but also of tenderness: “Fear not, little flock.”
observation: “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and keep it!” (11:28).
“Take care, and be on your guard against all covetousness, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions” (12:15).
“Fool! This night your soul is required of you” (12:20).
“Fear not, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom” (12:32).
“For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also” (12:34).
“Everyone to whom much was given, of him much will be required” (12:48).
“Unless you repent, you will all likewise perish” (13:3).
“It is like a grain of mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his garden” (13:19).
interpretation:
When Jesus casts out a demon, some say he does it by Beelzebul, and others ask for a sign. Jesus answers that a kingdom divided cannot stand, and that if he casts out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon them. There is no neutral ground: “Whoever is not with me is against me.” The only sign will be Jonah’s: his death and resurrection. A woman in the crowd calls out a blessing on his mother, and Jesus replies that those who hear and keep the word of God are blessed rather.

At a Pharisee’s meal, Jesus points out that cleaning the outside of the cup while the inside is full of greed is foolish. Six woes follow, to the Pharisees and to the lawyers. These are not words of hatred but of heartbreak for those who keep the outward forms and miss justice and the love of God.

Then he turns to the disciples: beware the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. Do not fear those who kill the body. God knows each sparrow, and you are of more value than many sparrows. Whoever acknowledges Christ before others will be acknowledged before the angels of God.

A man asks Jesus to settle an inheritance dispute, and Jesus tells of the rich fool, who stored up barns of grain and planned to relax, and heard, “Fool! This night your soul is required of you.” It is folly to be rich toward self and not rich toward God. He then tells the disciples not to be anxious: the ravens and lilies are cared for. “Fear not, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.” Sell, give, and lay up treasure in heaven.

The rest of the section calls for readiness: be dressed for action, like servants waiting for the master. Much given means much required. Jesus warns that he has come to bring division, and calls for repentance when tragedies occur. The fig tree is given one more year. A woman bent over for eighteen years is healed on the Sabbath, and Jesus calls her a daughter of Abraham. Two short parables close the section: the mustard seed and the leaven. The kingdom starts small and grows beyond expectation.
connection: Jonah 1 to 3 is the sign Jesus points to. Psalm 84:11 and Matthew 6:19-34 parallel his teaching on treasure and anxiety. Isaiah 5:1-7 is the background to the fig tree. Ecclesiastes 2 describes the vanity of laboring for riches. 1 Timothy 6:6-10 warns about the love of money. Hebrews 3:12-14 warns of the deceitfulness of sin. 1 Peter 5:7 says to cast all your anxieties on him.
application:
Look honestly at where your treasure is. What does your calendar and your bank statement say?

Name an anxiety you carry and give it to the Father who feeds the ravens.

Pray for readiness. If Jesus returned today, what would you want to have finished?
prayerPrompts: Confess where you store up for yourself and are not rich toward God.
Thank him for giving you the kingdom.
Ask him to loosen your grip on worry.
